keyframe_review.note: -333..-327 in Cliopatria: 1,558,417 km2, bbox 65.87-91.68E 20.02-31.01N, 6,029 cells. Cliopatria's shape reaches 65.87E and holds 515 of Sind's 562 cells, 97 of Baluchistan's and 128 of Pakistan's Punjab (740 cells in all) against a page that puts the west end at 'present-day Punjab' and has Alexander's army reach the Beas 'beyond which the Nanda territory was located'; the Alexander page has the 'Macedonian Empire annexes northwestern India' (Porus, Taxiles, the Malli, Sindh), so all of Pakistan is removed. Part of Pakistan's Punjab (Bahawalnagar-Cholistan) may lie east of the Sutlej-Beas line; it goes with the rest for simplicity (my reading, confidence 2). Corrected shape about 5,500 cells (1.39 M km2, ratio 0.89): Cliopatria's Nanda shape minus Pakistan, plus the Shaishunaga land of 345 (227 cells of that land lie outside Cliopatria's Nanda shape: 169 in Madhya Pradesh, the Malwa and Narmada country of Avanti, and about 45 in the Nepal Terai and hills of the Vajji polygon). The page gives no south limit beyond 'there is no concrete evidence that the Nanda rule extended to the south of the Vindhya range', and its north limit as 'extended up to the Ganges river in the present-day western Uttar Pradesh'; the shape's south edge (20.02N) and its reach over Rajasthan (1,346 of 1,353 cells), part of Gujarat and all of Bangladesh rest on no page opened. Their growth over the Shaishunaga shape is the ledger's -340 Kuru and Kalinga gains and the -333 remainder gain (confidence 1). The page gives no area, so there is no infobox figure to compare with Cliopatria's.

Cliopatria's Nanda shape holds 155 of Odisha's 568 cells, 137 of them outside the Shaishunaga land.

ledger.note: 333 BCE: the Nanda realm reaches its full extent in Cliopatria. About 3,060 cells (775,000 km2): Rajasthan 1,138, Madhya Pradesh 550, Uttar Pradesh 372, Chhattisgarh 154, Haryana 154, Bangladesh about 370, Indian Punjab 84, Gujarat 83, West Bengal 71. The page names the Haihaya country (the Narmada valley, 'capital at Mahishmati'), Mithila, Kashi, Vitihotra and Kosala and says the Nandas 'probably'/'may have' held them, all undated and none with a boundary, so the whole remainder is Cliopatria's shape at confidence 1 (the page is silent on the year and on every edge); it is the largest unverified area of the dossier.

region.text: the Nanda state in 322, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya

ledger.note: 322 BCE: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the last Nanda king, Dhana Nanda. 'The Nanda dynasty was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya, who was supported by his mentor (and later minister) Chanakya'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 322 BCE'. The page gives the year only in the infobox and no siege or battle date; the Alexander page also has 'Chandragupta Maurya of Magadha founded the Maurya Empire' at c. 322 BC. Cliopatria keeps the Nandas to -319.

wars.name: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory over the kings of the Punjab and the Indus; Alexander's army mutinied at the Hyphasis (Beas) 'refusing to march further east' and never met the Nandas, whose army the page calls 'five times the size of the Macedonian army'.
wars.note: Infobox '327–325 BC', result 'Macedonian victory', territorial changes 'Macedonian Empire annexes northwestern India'; the Nanda page puts the Beas in 'the summer of 326 BCE' with the Nanda territory beyond it. The Nandas were the expected opponent, not a belligerent: no zone is contested and the Nanda borders do not move (the Cliopatria edge in Pakistan is not a Nanda loss).

wars.name: Nanda conquests under Mahapadma
wars.outcome: The Nandas subjugate Pañcāla, Surasena and the Kuru country and the empire reaches 'from present-day Punjab in the west to Odisha in the east'.
wars.note: Undated: 'The Puranas state that the Nanda king Mahapadma destroyed the Kshatriyas, and attained undisputed sovereignty.' The years are the span from the founding to the last year before Cliopatria's Nanda shape; no contest events are written because the page gives no campaign or battle.

wars.name: Chandragupta Maurya's overthrow of the Nandas
wars.outcome: Chandragupta, supported by Chanakya, overthrows the Nanda dynasty (infobox c. 322 BCE) and the realm passes to the Maurya Empire.
wars.note: The page gives the year only in the infobox and, for the fighting, the Milinda Panha war between 'the Nanda general Bhaddasala (Sanskrit: Bhadrashala) and Chandragupta' and an unsuccessful early attack on the capital; no dated campaign, so no zone and no contest events. The dissolve carries the hand-over.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by a text or a survey: the page says the empire 'appears to have stretched' from Punjab to Odisha and that there is 'no concrete evidence' of rule south of the Vindhya. The west edge at the Beas (the Alexander page) is the firmest line.

sources.title: Nanda Empire
sources.note: Infobox (c. 345 - c. 322 BCE, Pataliputra), extent ('Punjab' to 'Odisha'), the conquests and their undated sources, Alexander at the Beas, the overthrow by Chandragupta; no area figure and no section headings in the copy received.

sources.title: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
sources.note: 327-325 BC, the Hydaspes in July 326 BC, the mutiny at the Hyphasis (Beas), 'Macedonian Empire annexes northwestern India', the satrapies and Chandragupta c. 322 BC; the Nanda mentions are in passing.

notes: Budget: two pages for three shapes. START AND END: Cliopatria has the row -333..-319; the infobox has c. 345..c. 322, so the dossier runs -345..-322 with a new keyframe for -345..-334 (the Shaishunaga state, whose own dossier ends -345) and the last shape cut to -322; the Maurya dossier should begin in -322 (Cliopatria's Maurya row begins -318). THE WEST: Cliopatria draws the Nanda realm to Sind and Baluchistan (65.87E); the Nanda page stops it at Punjab and the Alexander page at the Beas (all Pakistan removed, a reading of mine at confidence 2 recorded in the keyframes, not a ledger event). The 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' -326..-324 and 'Macedonian Empire' -323..-319 neighbours in the seed are Alexander's empire (the Ptolemaic row is a known mislabel), not a Nanda loss: no loss, contest or occupation event is written against them. THE GROWTH: the jump from the Shaishunaga shape to Cliopatria's 1.56 M km2 by -333 is explained only by confidence-1 gains of the Kuru disc and Odisha (both -340, the end of Mahapadma's reign, to whom the page's Puranic list credits the Kurus and Kalingas; moved from -333 by reviewer sa-01-d) and of the unnamed remainder (-333) (775,000 km2, mostly Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh), because the Nanda page's own conquest sentences are undated and hedged ('appears', 'may have', 'probably'). The reviewer should treat those three events as a gap to fill, and the south and east edges (Chhattisgarh, Bangladesh, Gujarat) as unverified. Not used: Asmaka (the page has only the theory 'Nau Nand Dehra'; neither Cliopatria shape contains the Asmaka disc; janapada-of-asmaka hands it to the Shaishunaga state in -345, which holds no such land here), the Haihaya country (Narmada valley, undated), Mithila (already inside Magadha), the Jain tradition that a Nanda minister 'subjugated the entire country up to the coastal areas' (no boundary), and the Kuntala (Karnataka) inscriptions, which the page calls 'not reliable'. No ruler strip: the page gives only Mahapadma 'c. 345 – c. 340 BCE' and Dhana Nanda 'c. 329 – c. 322 BCE' and says nine Nanda kings reigned. No new gazetteer names are needed here; 'Maheshwar' (place) is inherited from the Avanti hand-over region in the Shaishunaga land.
